caption: The drawing depicts a doorway set in a stone wall. The door itself is wooden, composed of two vertical panels with a natural wood grain pattern, colored in light to medium brown tones. The arched doorway features a decorative stone frame with alternating red and gray segments forming a zigzag pattern along the arch. Above the arch is a circular motif outlined in blue. On both sides of the arch, there are spiral and leaf-like decorative elements in red. The stone blocks making up the wall are outlined in blue-gray, with two horizontal decorative bands running across the lower portion of the wall. These bands contain repeating geometric and circular patterns in blue, yellow, white, and red orange colors. Below the bands, the lower wall is colored in red and ochre with a gradient effect, and the floor in front of the door consists of reddish-brown tiles. The artist’s signature, "R. Ruiz Taboada," is visible in red in the lower right corner of the drawing. The background is left empty, with no objects or detail beyond the doorway composition.
title: Wall Painting and Door (Interior)
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
